## Ansible host variables

is the set of Ansible variables cargoship reads for one host, as a type, so that a JSON Schema can be generated from it and an editor can complete and check a host_vars or group_vars file.

Rendered from `schema/ansible-hostvars-schema.json`.

<div class="schema-table">

| Property                       | Type                      | Required | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------- | -------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ansible_host`                 | `string`                  | no       |         | Address cargoship opens the SSH connection to. Defaults to the name the inventory knows the host by, which is the common shape.                                                                            |
| `ansible_port`                 | `string` or `integer`     | no       |         | Port cargoship connects on. Defaults to 22.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `ansible_ssh_private_key_file` | `string`                  | no       |         | Path to the SSH private key cargoship authenticates with.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `ansible_user`                 | `string`                  | no       |         | User cargoship connects as. Defaults to root.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `cargoship_bastion`            | [SSHConfig](#sshconfig)   | no       |         | Jump host cargoship reaches this node through. Cargoship does not parse ansible_ssh_common_args, so an inventory that reaches the fleet through a bastion for Ansible's own sake has to say so again here. |
| `cargoship_environment`        | map[string]`string`       | no       |         | Shell environment cargoship sets on the host, as a map of variable name to value.                                                                                                                          |
| `cargoship_files`              | array of [Files](#files)  | no       |         | Each entry is a file cargoship uploads to the host: src is a path on the management node, dst the path on the node.                                                                                        |
| `cargoship_host`               | [HostConfig](#hostconfig) | no       |         | Ports cargoship opens on this node, and the firewall rules it applies there.                                                                                                                               |
| `cargoship_hostname`           | `string`                  | no       |         | What the node calls itself, when that is not the name the inventory knows it by. Defaults to the inventory hostname.                                                                                       |
| `cargoship_node_labels`        | map[string]`string`       | no       |         | Kubernetes node labels applied to this node. A host setting this replaces its group's rather than adding to it.                                                                                            |
| `cargoship_node_taints`        | array of `string`         | no       |         | Kubernetes node taints applied to this node. A host setting this replaces its group's rather than adding to it.                                                                                            |
| `cargoship_private_address`    | `string`                  | no       |         | Address the cluster uses between nodes, when it is not the one cargoship would discover. A node with two interfaces is the usual reason.                                                                   |
| `cargoship_private_interface`  | `string`                  | no       |         | Interface the cluster uses between nodes, when it is not the one cargoship would discover.                                                                                                                 |
| `cargoship_profile`            | `string`                  | no       |         | Name of the profile this host selects. Defaults to the host's role, which is what makes the node-role.kubernetes.io/&lt;profile&gt; label say something.                                                   |
| `cargoship_profile_spec`       | [Profiles](#profiles)     | no       |         | Body of the profile this host selects, declared beside the selection. A profile defined twice with different bodies is an error naming both sources.                                                       |

</div>

### Files

defines a file to write to a host.

<div class="schema-table">

| Property | Type     | Required | Default | Description                                                     |
| -------- | -------- | -------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `data`   | `string` | no       |         | holds inline content for the file, as an alternative to Source. |
| `dst`    | `string` | no       |         | is the path on the host where cargoship writes the file.        |
| `dstDir` | `string` | no       |         | is the directory on the host where cargoship writes the file.   |
| `group`  | `string` | no       |         | identifies the file group on the host.                          |
| `name`   | `string` | yes      |         | identifies the file in the cluster configuration.               |
| `perm`   | `string` | no       |         | sets the file mode cargoship applies on the host.               |
| `src`    | `string` | no       |         | is the local path or URL cargoship reads the file from.         |
| `user`   | `string` | no       |         | identifies the file owner on the host.                          |

</div>

### FirewallConfig

is the backend-neutral firewall configuration for a node.

<div class="schema-table">

| Property | Type                                   | Required | Default | Description                                             |
| -------- | -------------------------------------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rules`  | array of [FirewallRule](#firewallrule) | no       |         | lists the firewall rules cargoship applies to the node. |

</div>

### FirewallPolicyConfig

configures a firewalld policy that opens ports from one zone to another.

<div class="schema-table">

| Property  | Type                                   | Required | Default | Description                                                                                            |
| --------- | -------------------------------------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Egress`  | [FirewallZone](#firewallzone)          | yes      |         | is the zone the policy allows traffic to.                                                              |
| `Ingress` | [FirewallZone](#firewallzone)          | yes      |         | is the zone the policy allows traffic from.                                                            |
| `ports`   | array of [FirewallPort](#firewallport) | no       |         | lists the ports this policy allows.                                                                    |
| `target`  | `string`                               | yes      |         | is the action taken on traffic that matches the policy. One of `CONTINUE`, `ACCEPT`, `REJECT`, `DROP`. |

</div>

### FirewallPort

defines a port allowed through the firewalld policy.

<div class="schema-table">

| Property   | Type                  | Required | Default | Description                                                          |
| ---------- | --------------------- | -------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `port`     | `string` or `integer` | yes      |         | is the port number, or port range, cargoship opens.                  |
| `protocol` | `string`              | yes      |         | is the type of allowed traffic. One of `tcp`, `udp`, `sctp`, `dccp`. |

</div>

### FirewallRule

is a single backend-neutral firewall rule.

<div class="schema-table">

| Property      | Type                  | Required | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------- | --------------------- | -------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `action`      | `string`              | yes      |         | is what cargoship does with traffic that matches the rule. One of `allow`, `deny`, `reject`.                                                                         |
| `destination` | `string`              | no       |         | is the address or CIDR the traffic goes to.                                                                                                                          |
| `direction`   | `string`              | no       | `in`    | selects which traffic the rule matches. It defaults to in. One of `in`, `out`, `forward`.                                                                            |
| `egress`      | `string`              | no       |         | names where forward traffic leaves. It is a zone on firewalld hosts and an<br>interface on ufw hosts. It applies to forward rules only.                              |
| `ingress`     | `string`              | no       |         | names where forward traffic enters. It is a zone on firewalld hosts and an<br>interface on ufw hosts. It applies to forward rules only.                              |
| `name`        | `string`              | no       |         | identifies the rule. Cargoship uses it to name the artifacts it writes on the<br>node, so it must be unique within a host. Cargoship generates one when it is empty. |
| `port`        | `string` or `integer` | no       |         | is the port number, or inclusive port range, the rule matches.                                                                                                       |
| `protocol`    | `string`              | no       |         | is the type of traffic the rule matches. One of `tcp`, `udp`, `sctp`, `dccp`.                                                                                        |
| `source`      | `string`              | no       |         | is the address or CIDR the traffic comes from.                                                                                                                       |

</div>

### FirewallZone

is the name of either the ingress or egress zone for a policy.

<div class="schema-table">

| Property | Type     | Required | Default | Description                    |
| -------- | -------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------ |
| `Name`   | `string` | yes      |         | identifies the firewalld zone. |

</div>

### HostConfig

defines the configuration for a specific host, including firewall policies and the ports cargoship opens on the node.

<div class="schema-table">

| Property   | Type                                                     | Required | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `firewall` | [FirewallConfig](#firewallconfig)                        | no       |         | holds the backend-neutral firewall rules cargoship renders onto whichever<br>firewall the node runs, firewalld, ufw, or nftables.                                                       |
| `policy`   | map[string][FirewallPolicyConfig](#firewallpolicyconfig) | no       |         | maps a policy name to a firewalld policy that allows traffic from one interface to another.<br>It is firewalld-only; prefer forward rules under `firewall.rules` for new configuration. |
| `ports`    | array of [HostPort](#hostport)                           | no       |         | lists the ports and protocols cargoship opens on the node.                                                                                                                              |

</div>

### HostEngine

defines configuration options for node-level metadata, specifically Kubernetes node labels and taints applied to a cluster host.

<div class="schema-table">

| Property | Type                | Required | Default | Description                                                     |
| -------- | ------------------- | -------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `labels` | map[string]`string` | no       |         | maps Kubernetes node label keys to their values.                |
| `taints` | array of `string`   | no       |         | lists the Kubernetes node taints cargoship applies to the node. |

</div>

### HostPort

is a port cargoship opens on the public side of the firewall.

<div class="schema-table">

| Property   | Type                  | Required | Default | Description                                          |
| ---------- | --------------------- | -------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `port`     | `string` or `integer` | yes      |         | is the port number, or port range, cargoship opens.  |
| `protocol` | `string`              | yes      |         | is the type of allowed traffic. One of `tcp`, `udp`. |

</div>

### Profiles

holds the host and engine overrides for one profile.

<div class="schema-table">

| Property      | Type                      | Required | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------- | ------------------------- | -------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `concurrency` | `string` or `integer`     | no       |         | limits how many hosts using this profile cargoship processes at once, e.g.<br>draining, upgrading, initializing, or uninstalling. It accepts a fixed count ("1") or a<br>percentage of the hosts sharing this profile ("25%"). Empty falls back to the phase's<br>default concurrency.                                                    |
| `engine`      | [HostEngine](#hostengine) | no       |         | holds the node label and taint overrides applied to a host that selects this profile.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `host`        | [HostConfig](#hostconfig) | no       |         | holds the configuration overrides applied to a host that selects this profile.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `inherit`     | `string`                  | no       |         | names another profile this one starts from. The settings here win, and anything this profile leaves empty is taken from the named one, which may itself inherit. Without it a cluster whose profiles differ in one field each has to spell every one of them out in full, which is how a profiles block grows faster than the fleet does. |

</div>
